reason: I1 is just a digital buffer/tap on net112 (LOGICQ1) and does not participate in the analog core that generates the internal decision nodes; removing it keeps the core operation intact but you lose that buffered logic output loading/isolation.
impact_estimate: Low (only affects availability/drive strength of LOGICQ1).

reason: I0 similarly buffers net104 (LOGICQ2) and is not required for the analog comparison/regeneration itself; deleting it preserves internal behavior but removes the dedicated logic-level output path and any load isolation it provided.
impact_estimate: Low (only affects availability/drive strength of LOGICQ2).

reason: M3 is a diode-connected PMOS (gate=drain at net93) that mainly serves as a bias/reference element for the resistive network (R2/R3) feeding the lower NMOS stages; removing it can still allow operation if net93 is biased elsewhere, but otherwise net93 may float and biasing becomes unreliable.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (safe only if net93 has an alternate bias path; otherwise operating point may drift or fail).
